title: Policy engine: routing & control-plane internals (multi-region, scoring, explainability)
body:
Purpose
This note captures internal design ideas and operational considerations for the Policy Evaluation Engine (PEE) when used by the routing/control-plane layer across multiple regions. Goal is to converge on a practical, debuggable runtime that: enforces constraints, computes a reproducible score for route selection, produces compact explainability logs, and supports safe, low-latency policy updates via the control plane.

Context / motivating problems
- Routing decisions need to respect hard constraints (region, model-variant compatibility, tenant SLAs) and optimize soft objectives (latency, cost, accuracy).
- The control plane must update policies frequently (canaries, experiments) with minimal disruption to route scoring semantics.
- Explainability and audit logs must be compact (to avoid egress costs) but actionable for troubleshooting and compliance.
- Multi-region topology introduces eventual-consistency trade-offs for policy updates and capacity signals.

Design principles
- Deterministic evaluation: given identical inputs and policy snapshot, scoring should be deterministic to help reproduce outcomes in postmortems.
- Two-tier constraints: enforce hard constraints early (filtering) then score remaining candidates by soft metrics.
- Versioned policy snapshots: control plane publishes immutable policy snapshots (policy-snap-<id>) used by edge evaluators.
- Graceful degradation: when a policy snapshot is unavailable or stale, fallback to last-known-good snapshot with explicit reason in explain log.
- Minimal, structured explain logs: one-line decision summary + optional top-3 contributing factors.

High-level flow (edge evaluator)
1) receive request context: tenant, target-region, feature-flags, cost-tier, request-hints (max-latency-ms, prefer-local)
2) fetch active policy snapshot id from local store (fast read path); if not present, query control-plane service with timeout
3) filter candidate endpoints by hard constraints (region, model compatibility, blacklists)
4) annotate candidates with runtime signals (queue depth, p99-latency, recent-failure-rate, capacity-score) from telemetry cache
5) compute normalized score per candidate: score = w_latency*norm(latency) + w_cost*norm(cost) + w_freshness*norm(version_age) + w_pref*policy_bias
6) pick winner (highest score) and secondary fallback list (n=2) for fast retry
7) emit explainability record and audit event; proceed to route request

Hard constraints vs soft constraints
- Hard constraints (reject candidate): region_allowed, tenant_policies (no-shared-infra), model_arch_compat, hardware_capability (nvlink, tensor cores), explicit_suspend flags
- Soft constraints (score penalty/bonus): observed_latency, cost_per_token_est, kv-cache-hit-rate, recent_success_rate, warm_state_score

Scoring model details
- Normalization: each metric is min-max normalized using sliding-window percentiles (5th-95th) to avoid outliers dominating. Store per-region normalization params and fall back to global if missing.
- Weights: policy defines weight vector per workload type (chat vs single-turn vs embedding). Weights can be tuned via control-plane experiments.
- Regularization: apply a small exploration epsilon to occasionally surface lower-cost candidates for learning. Controlled by per-tenant flag.
- Determinism: tie-break on candidate id and snapshot id to ensure reproducible ties.

Example pseudo-score (human readable)
- raw_latency_ms -> norm_latency = (p95_latency - 5th)/(95th-5th)
- raw_cost -> norm_cost scaled to [0,1]
- score = (0.5 * (1 - norm_latency)) + (0.3 * (1 - norm_cost)) + (0.2 * warm_state_score)

Policy snapshot model and control-plane integration
- Policy snapshot schema (high level): {snapshot_id, created_at, constraints[], scoring_profiles[], rollout_rules[], metadata}
- Control plane responsibilities: create snapshots (immutable), handle rollout rules (percent-of-traffic by tag), publish snapshot ids to region CDN (signed manifest), expose status API for rollout progress
- Edge behavior for rollouts: evaluator receives rollout token indicating which cohort it belongs to (percent hashing by tenant_id or request_id). Edge binds to snapshot id accordingly.
- Canary updates: support staged rollout where scoring_profiles can be marked canary=true and include a canary_end_time. After expiry, canary either promoted or garbage-collected.

Multi-region concerns
- Replication lag: policy snapshots replicate via a push CDN with strong ordering per-snapshot id but not strict global linearizability. Snapshot ids carry monotonic sequence numbers per region to detect misses.
- Regional overrides: allow per-region scoring overrides for local cost/latency characteristics. Merge rule: region-overrides take precedence for soft weights; constraints merge OR (must satisfy global && region constraints).
- Fallback on region split: when region health is degraded, control-plane can signal temporary constraints (e.g., route-out-of-region-allowed = false). Edges must honor immediately.

Explainability / audit log format
- Keep small: single-line CSV-like summary per request + optional detailed blob for sampled requests.
- Fields (compact): ts, tenant, req_id, snapshot_id, winner_id, score (three-decimal), reason_codes (semi-colon), fallback_list (ids), decision_latency_ms
- Example: 2025-01-24T15:11:03Z,acme,req-1234,SNAP-765,rt-12,0.827,REGION_OK;MODEL_MATCH;WARM_HIT,rt-11|rt-9,12
- Detailed blob (sampled): includes per-candidate metric vector, normalization params used, policy snippet id, telemetry hash. Store these in a separate cold store and link by event id.

Privacy & compliance notes
- Avoid logging tenant PII. Mask any prompt metadata in explain blobs. Use deterministic hashing for identifiers when required by compliance.
- Access controls: audit logs must be queryable by customer for their tenants only. Provide retention knobs.

Observability and alerting
- Key metrics to emit per-region and per-snapshot: decision-rate, fallback-rate, mean-score, top-failure-reasons, snapshot-miss-rate, snapshot-staleness-distribution
- Alerts: snapshot-miss-rate > 1% sustained, fallback-rate > 3x baseline, explain-sample-variance spike (indicates a scoring drift)
- Dashboards: snapshot rollout heatmap (percent-of-traffic by snapshot), per-tenant mean-score, top policies causing rejects

Operational playbooks (brief)
- If policy rollout causes high fallbacks: rollback snapshot to previous snapshot id, inspect explain-sample blobs for top reason codes, check region override deltas
- If snapshot missing in a region: fail-open to last-known-good snapshot and create incident to push snapshot via control-plane secondary channel
- If explain logs show privacy leakage: pause explain sampling, rotate masking rules, notify compliance

Open questions / TODOs
- How to version normalization params safely across snapshots so edge evaluators reproduce identical normalization? (Option: include normalization stat summary in snapshot metadata)
- Do we allow runtime feature-flags from experiments to override scoring weights? (Risk: non-determinism across replicas)
- Policy size vs push latency: large snapshots can slow rollout. Consider delta encoding for snapshots and streaming apply.

Appendix: short checklist for implementers
- [ ] implement deterministic tie-breaking using snapshot id + candidate id
- [ ] include normalization summary in snapshot metadata (p5, p95) for each metric
- [ ] emit compact explain event for every request and sample detailed blob at 0.1%
- [ ] support region overrides with explicit merge semantics
- [ ] add control-plane api: POST /snapshots, GET /snapshots/:id/status, POST /rollouts

Notes history
- 2025-01-14 initial draft by Aisha
- 2025-01-20 added scoring normalization proposal (Marcelo)
- 2025-01-28 added explain log compact format and sampling rules (Jia)
- 2025-02-03 updated multi-region rollouts and checklist (Tom)
